dossier.claim: Quotation boundaries and sentence typography repeatedly fail at the point where the reader must distinguish speech from narration or one sentence from the next.
dossier.sourcePattern: The cited speech ends before narration, continues past an intermediate paragraph, or belongs wholly to one speaking turn. Other examples contain ordinary consecutive sentences rather than a joined word or doubled terminal period.
dossier.englishEffect: Completed dialogue is left unclosed, a continuous explanation closes early, and narration acquires an orphaned closing quote. Double-quoted speech sometimes ends with an apostrophe. “Body.It,” “body.Someone,” and “thing.Are” fuse sentence boundaries, while a doubled period leaves a minor terminal typo.
dossier.limits: A missing closing quote at an intermediate paragraph of continuing speech is conventional English punctuation, not an error. Interrupted source utterances and deliberate ellipses require their own context. Only intact extraction rows support these findings. A recoverable punctuation typo is not automatically a changed speaker or a serious semantic error.
dossier.diagnostic: 77 findings in this category; 8 cited passages.
